problems.statement: Going back to 8-hour shifts is the fix (12-hour shift fatigue is the cause of the yield decline).
The Corvane bar change (hardness scatter widened further after the 1 Sept billet source change) is a material contributor to the Line 3 yield loss and to Halvard journal-diameter rejects.

Deferred quarterly spindle service (no service since May; runout and vibration drifting, worst on L3-02 and L3-05) is a material contributor to the yield loss, especially on the tight-tolerance long shaft.

The decline is multi-causal: steel variability and spindle wear, both made possible by cost and backlog pressure decisions made without checking effects, interact and cannot be separated with current Line 3 data because they changed together.
The nine new, shortened-training operators are the cause of the decline.
The yield drop is an inspection or measurement artifact (CMM, gauge, criteria or program change).
The scrap tag timing in the last hours of shift shows fatigue-driven defects at shift end.
Higher wear-offset keying and insert changes by operators (a downstream effect of chatter or wear) add error and are a mediating path rather than an independent root cause.

Management decisions (cost saving on steel, deferring maintenance for backlog, no Line 3-specific traceability) removed the safeguards that would have shown the cause; Line 3 now carries a real customer-quality risk (Halvard PPM up, containment due 13 Nov).

causalClaims.to: Increased journal-size scatter, chatter and rejects
Increased size scatter and rejects, especially on L3-02 and L3-05

causalClaims.from: Higher reject rate in Line 3 sequence C-05 to C-10 vs C-01 to C-04
Worn spindle or wider hardness scatter
causalClaims.to: More insert changes and manual offset entry

actions.action: Do the deferred spindle service now, two machines at a time on weekend 12-hour shifts, starting with L3-02 and L3-05, and record before/after runout and reject rates.
actions.rationale: It is cheap, overdue, and the backlog (1.2 weeks) no longer makes it a shipment risk; it also tests the spindle explanation.

actions.action: Pull CMM results for the roughly 1,400 Corvane long shafts run on the serviced, 8-hour-shift Line 6 lathe and compare with L3-02 and L3-05.
actions.rationale: It is the only existing natural experiment separating Corvane bar from a worn spindle and shift length, at near-zero cost.

actions.action: Run the Tamsworth trial lots (available within 10 days) on Line 3 in a planned comparison against Corvane, ideally crossed with serviced vs unserviced machines, and begin matching lathe cycle counters to CMM serials.
actions.rationale: Breaks the confounding of steel and spindle condition and gives the first time-of-cut traceability.

actions.action: Return Line 3 to 8-hour shifts, but present it as a risk and capacity decision rather than as the confirmed fix, and do not rely on it to restore yield.
actions.rationale: The customer accepts 8-hour capacity for the backlog and staff are split on shifts, but the evidence does not tie yield loss to shift length, and the change alone would likely leave steel and spindle issues unfixed.

actions.action: Send Halvard an interim containment and root-cause plan: 100% inspection kept, a hold on suspect Corvane lots, and a Corvane request for billet-source and hardness data.
actions.rationale: The scorecard deadline has passed or is imminent and the Halvard reject rate (290 PPM) is a real customer risk.

actions.action: Cut Line 3 final CMM inspection from 100% to 1-in-10 sampling.
actions.rationale: Rejects are doubling and Halvard PPM is climbing; reducing detection while the cause is unknown would push more defects to the customer.

actions.action: Adopt the Corvane 7.5% saving as permanent.
actions.rationale: Corvane's source changed on 1 Sept with wider hardness scatter, and the steel has not been ruled out as a cause.

actions.action: Retrain, restrict or blame the nine new operators.
actions.rationale: Their reject rates equal those of experienced operators and the decline began before they ran alone.

actions.action: Add a hardness-spread (SD) check to incoming inspection, and add lot and cycle-count traceability from lathe to CMM serial.
actions.rationale: The spec only checks individual readings; spread control and traceability close the detection gaps that hid this problem.

nextEvidence: CMM journal-diameter results for the ~1,400 Corvane long shafts made on the serviced Line 6 lathe, compared with L3-02 and L3-05.
Before/after results of spindle service on Line 3 (runout, vibration, reject rate) and Tamsworth trial-lot yield on Line 3 machines.
Lathe cycle-counter logs (180-day retention) matched to CMM serials to give reject by time-of-cut, shift hour and machine, and Corvane's billet-source and hardness-spread data.
output.summary: The Plant Manager's belief that 12-hour shifts caused the yield drop is not supported. Scrap tag times reflect batch-writing, not when the defect occurred, and the decline began in week 32 with the Corvane bar, before the 12-hour pattern. New operators and CMM measurement are ruled out. The two live causes are Corvane bar with widening hardness spread and deferred spindle service (runout rising, worst on L3-02/L3-05). They changed together on Line 3 and cannot yet be separated. Service the spindles, pull the Line 6 Corvane results, and run Tamsworth trials. Reverting to 8-hour shifts is acceptable but unconfirmed as a fix. Avoid sampling inspection and permanent Corvane adoption.
